newsitem.title: GREECE: SOCCER-GREECE AIM TO END CROATIA'S WORLD CUP HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GREECE AIM TO END CROATIA'S WORLD CUP HOPES.

text.p: Greece need to win their World Cup qualifier on Wednesday to turn group one into a straight duel between themselves and Denmark but they are expecting opponents Croatia to put up a fight.
"We want one of the two top positions in our group," Greek coach Costas Polychroniou told a joint news conference with Croatian coach Miloslav Blasevic.
"If we win, Croatia will be literally out of the race and Denmark will be the only ones chasing us. The Croats play their last card in Salonika and I expect a difficult match," he said.
Blasevic said the Croats were determined to get a good result from Wednesday's match.
"We came to fight for a good result. If we don't win we lose everything," he said.
Polychroniou said Greece wanted three wins from their remaining three matches "so that we qualify on our own and don't depend on the results of the others".
Greece, who scored a precious 1-0 away win in Bosnia earlier this month, will be without defender Yannis Kalitzakis, who is suspended. Otherwise they are at full strength.
Top Greek league scorers Demis Nikolaidis and Costas Franzeskos will lead the Greek attack while suspended defender Nikos Dabizas returns.
"We will attack from the start. As in every other match our aim is an early goal. The Croats are very fast and talented and dangerous in counter-attacks," Polychroniou said.
Croatia have drafted two Zagreb-based defenders into their side.

Goran Juiric will win his second cap by replacing injured Nikola Jerkan in the libero position while Croatia Zagreb team mate Dario Simic is expected to play in the heart of the defence alongside Slaven Bilic of England's West Ham.
Zvonimir Soldo of Germany's VfB Stuttgart, who played in Croatia's 3-3 draw against Slovenia earlier this month, will move into midfield.
In attack, Blazevic will be able to field Alen Boksic of Juventus, who has fully recovered from a recent injury, and Real Madrid's top scorer Davor Suker.
Croatia have six points from four matches and badly need a win on Wednesday.

Greece - Ilias Atmatzidis, Stratos Apostolakis, Michalis Kasapis, Kyriakos Karataidis, Marinos Ouzounidis, Nikos Dabizas, Costas Frantzeskos, Ilias Poursanidis, Thodoros Zagorakis, George Donis, Demis Nikolaidis
Croatia - Tonci Gabric, Zvonimir Soldo, Goran Juiric, Robert Jarni, Dario Simic, Slaven Bilic, Svonimir Boban, Robert Prosinecki, Aljosa Asanovic, Davor Suker, Alen Boksic.
